 UEFA Nations League
 Bellamy demands Wales turns moments into results
 Craig Bellamy urged his Wales team to end its disappointing Nations League campaign on a high ahead of its final Group A4 clash against Portugal on Wednesday.

 Wales is already confirmed to finish bottom of the group after a 3-1 defeat to Norway last time out, with Portugal's spot in the quarter-finals of the competition also sealed. 
 However, Portugal comes into the clash off the back of a 4-1 loss against Denmark in their first match since Cristiano Ronaldo announced his international retirement. 
 This is the first time Wales will host Portugal for a match since May 1951, when it won 2-1 in a friendly at Ninian Park thanks to goals from Mal Griffiths and Trevor Ford.
 But Bellamy's side comes into the game having lost four of their last five competitive matches, which is as many defeats as it suffered across its previous 25 between March 2023 and March 2026.
 Its only win in the Nations League came against Norway on 1 October, though its biggest defeats in the competition this year have only been by a two-goal margin. 
 Portugal has won four of its five matches against Wales in all competitions, including the last three in a row without conceding a goal, and Bellamy insisted an encounter with Jorge Jesus's side is the perfect way for his team to bounce back.
 "Playing against the best [in League A of the Nations League], you feel this is exactly the game you need to be in; you just feel this is how you get close to them," Bellamy said.
 "But now it's about turning these moments into winning these games. It's a big ask we know, but I feel not too far away from that.
 "Portugal are very aggressive; they will be on the front foot. The quality they have, we know. But [the key] for us is to always [be putting] pressure on the ball.
 "We have to stay together, we have to be compact, so for us, it's just trying to keep the best version of ourselves."
 Wales lost 1-0 to Denmark in its last home Nations League game – it has never lost consecutive home games in the competition, while it last did so in competitive games in defeats to Croatia and Serbia in March and September 2013 respectively.
 Portugal could still finish second should its lose at the Cardiff City Stadium on Wednesday and Denmark beat Norway, but the Selecao will be confident of getting the job done. 
 It has won 12 of its last 16 competitive away matches, and has lost just three of its last 26 on the road in competitive fixtures.
 "It's another very tough test against a very good side but we want to show that we are more than capable of competing with top-quality nations," Wales defender Ben Davies said.
 "A couple of games on another day could have gone our way and the next step for us is turning those good performances into results."
 While Wales is consigned to a bottom-place finish in the group, it could still avoid relegation from the top tier if it wins its relegation play-off in March.
